# Set up
1. Load the tidyverse library. 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

2. Load the billboard data. 
```{r}
data("billboard")
```

3. Describe the dataset. 
Song rankings for Billboard top 100 in 2000. The dataset contains artist name, song name, date the song enter the top 100, and the rank of the song each week after it entered.

4. Print the column names from this dataset. 
```{r}
colnames(billboard)
```

5. Print the first 5 entries in the dataset. 
```{r}
head(billboard, n = 5)
```


# Practice
1. Create a subset of data that has Jay-Z as the only artist. How many songs are in it?
```{r}
jayz <- billboard %>% filter(artist == "Jay-Z")
```

2. In the original dataset, use filter to find information about the song "All the small things." What was the highest position (i.e. lowest number) this song reached on the billboard 100? 
```{r}
all_small <- billboard %>% filter(track == "All The Small Things")
range(all_small[,4:50], na.rm = TRUE)
```

3. Create a subset of data for songs Tim McGraw sang. Summarize the data for wk 1.
```{r}
tim_mcgraw_dat <- billboard %>% filter(artist == "McGraw, Tim")

summary(tim_mcgraw_dat$wk1)
```

4. Create a function that can be used to determine if Britney Spears sang the song. 
```{r}
did_britney <- function(song_name){
  artist <- billboard$artist[billboard$track == song_name][1]
  
  if (artist == "Spears, Britney"){
    paste("yes")
  } else {
    paste("no")
  }
}
```

5. Test your function on the billboard data. Save the results to a new column called "wasItBritney"
```{r}
billboard$was_it_britney <- NA

for (i in 1:nrow(billboard)) {
  billboard$was_it_britney[i] <- did_britney(billboard$track[i])
}
```

6. Use a for loop to determine if a song placed 50 or below or placed above 50 during the first week. 
```{r}
for (i in 1:nrow(billboard)) {
  if (billboard$wk1[i] <= 50) {
    cat(billboard$track[i], "- 50 or below\n")
  } else {
    cat(billboard$track[i], "- above 50\n")
  }
}
```

7. Use an if else statement to determine the same information as you obtained with the for loop. 
```{r}
first_week_place <- function(song_name) {
  for (i in 1:nrow(billboard)) {
    if (billboard$track[i] == song_name) {
      if (billboard$wk1[i] <= 50) {
        return("50 or below")
      }
      return("above 50")
    }
  }
  "song not found"
}
```

8. Compare your results in 6 and 7. 
```{r}
first_week_place("Kryptonite")
```
The if else statement I made searches for one song, while the loop goes through all the songs in the billboard dataset and returns a value for each one.
